Health Information Systems

Health information systems — HIS modules, EHR, PACS, RIS and benefits in hospitals.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • List modules of a hospital information system
  • Describe the electronic health record
  • State benefits of health information systems

In simple words

Health information systems (HIS) are computer systems that manage health data in hospitals and clinics. They connect departments and improve care coordination.

Key systems: hospital information system (HIS), electronic health record (EHR), picture archiving (PACS), radiology information (RIS), laboratory information (LIS).

HIS modules

Module Function
Patient registration Admission, demographics
Electronic health record Clinical notes, results, orders
Pharmacy Medication orders, dispensing
Laboratory Test orders and results
Radiology (PACS/RIS) Images and reports
Billing Charges and payments

Electronic health record (EHR)

An EHR is a digital version of a patient’s chart. It includes history, diagnoses, medicines, allergies, immunisations, results and notes. It is accessible to authorised providers.

Benefits

  • Legible, complete records.
  • Quick access to results and history.
  • Fewer duplicate tests.
  • Better coordination between departments.
  • Data for reporting and quality improvement.

🔴 EHR is the digital chart

The EHR is the patient’s digital chart — history, diagnoses, medicines, allergies, results and notes — accessible to authorised providers.

Where the nurse uses this

  • Document in the EHR — chart notes, vital signs and care in real time.
  • View results — check lab and imaging results as soon as available.
  • Medication orders — receive and process electronic orders and alerts.
  • Coordinate care — share information with other departments and providers.
  • Protect access — log in with your own ID; view only what you need for care.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. HIS modules: registration, EHR, pharmacy, laboratory, radiology, billing.
  2. The EHR is the digital patient chart — history, diagnoses, medicines, allergies, results, notes.
  3. Benefits: legible records, quick access, fewer duplicate tests, better coordination.
  4. Nurses document and view results in the EHR.
  5. Protect access — your own ID, view only what you need.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. PACS stores and displays radiology images.
  2. LIS manages laboratory orders and results.
  3. EHR supports decision-making and care coordination.
  4. Report system problems to IT support.

📌 Memory trick

HIS modules: “R-E-P-L-R-B” — Registration, EHR, Pharmacy, Laboratory, Radiology, Billing.

60-second revision

  • HIS connects hospital departments via computer.
  • Modules: registration, EHR, pharmacy, laboratory, radiology, billing.
  • EHR = digital patient chart.
  • Benefits: legible records, quick access, coordination.
  • Nurse: document, view results, process orders, protect access.

Test yourself

EHR stands for:

Answer: A. EHR = Electronic Health Record — the digital patient chart.

PACS is used in:

Answer: B. PACS (Picture Archiving and Communication System) stores radiology images.

A benefit of HIS is:

Answer: B. HIS reduces duplicate tests by sharing results across departments.

Nurses should access the EHR:

Answer: B. Access only the records of patients you are caring for.

Billing module handles:

Answer: B. The billing module manages patient charges and payments.
